

  On the question “Shall the House concur in the Senate amendment
H–8459?” (H.F. 1003)

   The ayes were, 57:

Barker              Behn               Bergan          Blom
Bloomingdale        Boden              Bossman         Bradley
Cisneros            Collins            Determann       Dunwell
Fett                Fisher             Gehlbach        Gerhold
Golding             Grassley, Spkr.    Gustoff         Harris
Hayes               Henderson          Hermanson       Holt
Hora                Ingels             Jeneary         Johnson, C.
Jones               Kaufmann           Kniff McCulla   Larson
Lawler              Lohse              Lundgren        Meggers
Meyer, A.           Mohr               Mommsen         Moore
Nordman             Sieck              Siegrist        Sitzmann
Smith               Stone              Thompson        Thomson
Vondran             Watkins            Weldon          Wengryn
Williams            Windschitl         Wood            Young
Wills,
 Presiding

   The nays were, 28:

Baeth               Bagniewski         Brown-Powers    Cooling
Croken              Ehlert             Gosa            Jacoby
Johnson, R.         Judge              Konfrst         Kressig
Kurth               Levin              Madison         Matson
McBurney            Meyer, B.          Nielsen         Ramirez
Sorensen            Srinivas           Turek           Wessel-Kroeschell
Wichtendahl         Wilburn            Wilson          Zabner

   Absent or not voting, 15:

Amos Jr.            Andrews            Dieken          Gaines
Gearhart            Gjerde             James           Latham
Olson               Rinker             Scholten        Shipley
Wheeler             Wilz               Wulf


  The motion prevailed and the House concurred in the Senate
amendment H–8459.

   Barker of Story moved that the bill, as amended by the Senate and
concurred in by the House, be read a last time now and placed upon its
passage which motion prevailed and the bill was read a last time.
1092                           JOURNAL OF THE HOUSE                 111th Day



   On the question “Shall the bill pass?” (H.F. 1003)

   The ayes were, 85:

   The nays were, none.


   Absent or not voting, 15:

Amos Jr.            Andrews            Dieken         Gaines
Gearhart            Gjerde             James          Latham
Olson               Rinker             Scholten       Shipley
Wheeler             Wilz               Wulf


  The bill having received a constitutional majority was declared to
have passed the House and the title was agreed to.

                          CONSIDERATION OF BILLS
                           Ways and Means Calendar

   House File 2785, a bill for an act extending the biodiesel blended
fuel tax credit, was taken up for consideration.
111th Day                      SATURDAY, MAY 2, 2026                         1093



   Vondran of Scott moved that the bill be read a last time now and
placed upon its passage which motion prevailed and the bill was read
a last time.
